29th Division left Brittany on 24 September to rejoin First Army and its command post is next listed in the Netherlands on 29 September (rail and motor move of about 800 km).
6th Armored Division moved from Brittany to the Third Army front in Lorraine in mid-September; the Green Book gives the move and the CMH list dates the two command posts.

7th Armored Division, landed at Omaha Beach, was ordered on 13 August to pass through Le Mans to La Ferté-Bernard and on 14 August to attack toward Dreux; the Green Book describes the hurried road march.
Panzer Lehr was ordered up on 7 June for a 90-mile drive from the Chartres area to the Thury-Harcourt assembly areas (documented relocation in C0038).

Pont-l'Abbé here is the hamlet astride Picauville and Étienville (Manche); the stored point is the Étienville commune centroid. The one stored geocoder candidate for the name is Pont-l'Abbé in Finistère, 265 km away, a namesake.

Map row C6058 (12th Army Group situation map, 27 February 1945) puts the LXIII Corps at Freiburg im Breisgau; Stacey (p. 495; C7510) has the 63rd Corps holding the First Parachute Army left to south of Roermond on 25 February. The map symbol is probably stale or misread; both rows kept, roadmap 247.

The 12th Army Group map row C4949 (2 January 1945) still shows the 7th Parachute Division on the Maas, probably a stale symbol; B-262 (C7925) has the division leave for the Strasbourg area at the end of December and C1106 has it fighting at Hatten on 10 January 1945, so the apparent 324 km move in two days is a map lag, not a move.

The 12th Army Group map row C6166 (6 March 1945) still has the 245th Infantry Division near Mertzwiller in Alsace; B-414 (C7950, German p.5) has it in Army Group H reserve about Coesfeld 'since 5 March'. One of the two is a map lag or an approximate date in a postwar manuscript; both rows kept, roadmap 266.

Different representative points: C7967 is the Army Group H front line of 30/31 March (IJssel-Lochem-Rheine) at Lochem, C7943 the army group command post moved to north-west of Bersenbrück on 31 March (Anlage 6); not a move of one body.

C1223 (6 April) places the creation of Army Blumentritt at a representative point for north-west Germany; C7971 is the staff's command post at Celle about 7 April (B-414 p.24, Skizze 5); the distance is between a regional point and a command post, not a move.

C7603 (17 April) is the II Parachute Corps front on the Küstenkanal; C7979 (18 April) is the operational area Cuxhaven-Bremerhaven toward which its move north begins (Skizze 6, note 6); the row marks the destination area, not a one-day move.

The 12th Army Group map row C6032 (27 February 1945) has the 245th Infantry Division near Mertzwiller in Alsace; B-147 (C8001) has it arriving about Borken to refit in the first days of March (date approximate). A move by rail between the two is possible over the gap but the map symbol may lag; both rows kept, roadmap 266.

C4779 is the 12th Army Group map row of 19 December 1944 that still shows the 59th Infantry Division in Holland (map lag: B-811, C2130, has it arriving north of Heinsberg on 4 December); C8064 (about 20 December, place inferred) has it relieving the 340th Volksgrenadier Division in the Roer sector.

167th Volksgrenadier Division was carried by rail from Piešťany (Slovakia) to the West from 14 December 1944 and arrives at Gerolstein on 24 December (rail move of about 830 km; theater and placeholder pass, 9 November 2026).
